title: 001 - A private conversation
content:
要求
  内化单词 + 语法 + 习惯用法。 听力 + 口语 + 写作练习     Bilibili
 课前问题      [[how-to-create-a-sentence|如何根据格式造句]]  1. 课文     Last week, I went to the theater. I had a very good seat.
The play was interesting. But I did not enjoy it.
A young man and a young woman were sitting behind me. They were talking loudly.
I got very angry. I could not hear the actors.
I turned around. I looked at the man and the woman, but they did not pay any attention.
In the end, I could not bear it.
I turned around again. “I can’t hear a word”, I said angrily.
“It’s none of your business.” the young man said. “This is a private conversion!”
2. Vocabulary      每个单词造句 5 句
   private (adj.) + n. / privately (adv.) + v.
 private book, private conversation, private stuff, private discuss … private a school - (NCE1L55) 私立学校； go to a private school He talks to her privately. (他们俩私下交谈) He goes to a private school. Does he go to a private school? When did he go to a private school? With whom does he go to a private school?  He goes to a private school with Tom. Who does he go to a private school with?   He was studying in a private school. He had studied in a private school.    conversation(n.) 谈话， 对话
 This is a private conversation. Is this a private conversation. Does he have a business conversation with Jeniffer? Who hosts the conversation? The conversation has been closed concluded. （完成式+被动） Has the conversation been concluded? This conversation is over.    theater (n. 美), theatre(n. 英) , cinema (n.)
 在英语中，当我们说“去剧院（看戏）”或“在剧院里”时，通常需要定冠词 the。这是一个固定搭配。 Tom invites his girlfriend to go to the theater.  Tom is planning to take his girlfriend to the theater this weekend. (使用“take sb. to”比“go to with sb.”更显主动和安排)   During the dating, Tom and his girlfriend watched saw a play in the theater.  see a play 观剧 (固定搭配)   When did they go to the theater? Have you ever gone been to the theater? (完成时+疑问句)  动词选择： Have you ever gone... 语法正确，但 Have you ever been... 是询问“经历”时更标准、更地道的说法。   The theater had been closed down. (剧场已经关张了。 过去完成式+被动)  close down 特指“永久关闭、歇业”      [[seat|seat 常见表达式]]
  play (n.) 话剧
 Do you like the play? The play they discussed, The Hamlet, is about revenge. (主语，同位语)  结构优秀： 你成功使用了定语从句 (they discussed) 和同位语 (The Hamlet)。这是高分句型！ 细节修正： 剧名《哈姆雷特》通常不加定冠词，就是 Hamlet。同位语前后通常用逗号隔开。 The play they discussed, Hamlet, is essentially a revenge tragedy. (使用“revenge tragedy复仇悲剧”这个更准确的文学术语)   I was a member of play club drama club in high school. (play club 名词短语) What’s the play about?  Could you give me a brief synopsis of the play? (使用 synopsis 摘要，更正式)   Why did you not like this play? Why didn’t you like this play? It’s a worldwide famous play. (世界著名的话剧)  It’s a world-renowned play. (最标准、最稳妥的书面表达) It’s a world-famous play. (最直接的表达，完全正确)      loudly (adv.) -> talk loudly
 They were talking loudly. They young couple argue loudly, it must be heard in anywhere of this building. (must + 动词 = 肯定推测。 夸张用法，表现吵架激烈程度)  句式错误： 这是两个完整的句子，不能用逗号连接，这是“逗号粘连”错误。 用词优化： in anywhere 不正确。Anywhere 是副词，前面不加介词。应改为 anywhere in this building。   The young couple argue so loudly that they must be audible anywhere in the building. (用“so…that…”正确连接两句，用更正式的“audible”替换“heard”)   The bell immediately rings loudly at the time of diamond stolen. (钻石刚被偷，立马铃声大作)  表达冗余 at the time of diamond stolen 是中文直译，不地道。   用词精度： “钻石被偷”是一个事件，最好用从句或名词化结构。   The alarm bell rang loudly the moment the diamond was stolen. (用“the moment”引导时间状语从句，非常简洁有力)   “Pay attention,” the headmaster speak loudly. They discussed loudly.    angry (adj.) , angrily (adv.)
 I look at her angrily. Do you look at her angrily? She felt angrily angry cause because her child broke the vest again.  词性错误（核心）： felt 是系动词（感觉起来），后面应接形容词 angry 作表语，描述主语的状态，而不是副词 angrily。副词修饰的是动作“如何感觉”，这不符合逻辑。 ❌ She felt angrily. (她“感觉”的方式是生气地？不通。) ✅ She felt angry. (她感到很生气。) 连词错误： cause 表示“导致”，是动词。这里需要表示“因为”的连词，应是 because。   It’s very dangerous driving angrily. (路怒症很危险) What makes him angry?    attention (n.) -> pay attention
 She didn’t pay any attention to my warning. Do you pay any attention in class? He has payed paid attention to his teacher. Has he paid attention to his teacher?  He has been paying attention to his teacher lately. (使用现在完成进行时 has been paying，强调从过去持续到现在的关注行为)   Panda is payed attention from tourists. (熊猫被游客关注着。)   pay attention 这个短语通常不用被动语态 Pandas are a major focus of attention for tourists. (使用 are a focus of attention 是关注的焦点，是更书面的好表达)      bear (v.) -> bore (过去分词) -> borne (过去分词) , boring(现在分词)
 I could not bear it. (原文) I can’t bear it. （同义词替换） Can you bear that? How can you bear that? （提问） He bore his unlucky life. (时态， 他忍受了他不幸的生活) Last year, he was unlucky, but he had borne it. (完成式)    business (n.)
 It’s none of your business. 与你无关。 It’s not my business. 与我无关。  That’s not my concern. (更正式一点) I don’t want to get involved. (我不想掺和。)   He is a businessman / she is a businesswoman商人 He had been a businessman last year. Business is business. Never explain your excuse again.  Remember, business is business. We can’t let friendship affect this decision.      rudely (adv.) , rude (adj.)
  “Get off the room”, the man said rudely.
  Tom splashes slapped the girl rudely. (他粗鲁的删了女孩耳光)
 splash water 溅水    Percy Buttons is rejected rudely. (Percy 被粗鲁地拒绝了)
 Percy Buttons was rudely turned away. (使用短语动词 turn away 拒之门外，比 reject 更有画面感)    Maybe he’s not choice to be husband, he must give up if you treated him rudely. (must +do = 肯定推测， if + did 假设条件)
批改：
  这是一个非常好的复合句尝试！ 包含了“推测”和“条件假设”。但有几个关键错误：
 用词错误： he's not choice ❌。Choice 是名词“选择”。这里想说“他可能不是（做）丈夫的（好）人选”。正确说法是：he might not be husband material 或 he may not be the right choice for a husband。 run-on sentence： 两个完整的独立句子（Maybe...husband 和 he must...rudely）不能用逗号连接。 虚拟语气混淆： 你的注释“if + did 假设条件”是对的，但主句的 must give up 是直陈语气，表示“必须放弃”。在非真实条件句中（尤其与未来可能相反），主句常用 would/might/should + 动词原形。 逻辑主语： he must give up 是谁放弃？是“他”放弃，还是“你”放弃追求他？根据句意，似乎是“你”应该放弃他。  提升版（厘清逻辑后）：
  Maybe he’s not husband material. He would probably give up on you if you treated him rudely. (拆成两句，第二句使用虚拟条件句 would give up if treated，逻辑是“他会放弃你”。) If you were to treat him rudely, he would likely lose interest. After all, he might not be the right choice for you. (使用 If you were to... 的虚拟结构，更正式；并重新组织了逻辑。) He must not be a good choice as a husband if he gives up simply because you were rude to him once. (将整个句子重组，用 must not be 表示对现在的否定推测，条件句用直陈语气，表达一种真实可能的情况。)         4. Expression (常用表达)      造句指南
 动词变化 （时态变化） 四句型变化 （陈述句 / 一般疑问句 Do / 特殊疑问句 How, where, when, who )   方式/地点/时间     其他习惯用法     其他单词 （词语组合） 1. 名词 -> adj. + n. 2. 动词 -> v. + adv. 3. …   原文摘抄+变化    loudly   In a loud voice: 用大声地（描述说话方式） Raise one’s voice: 提高嗓门 At the top of one’s lungs: 声嘶力竭地（程度最强） Deafeningly: 震耳欲聋地（修饰声音本身）   go to the theater  I had to go the the theater yesterday. Did you have to go to the theater yesterday? Why did you have to go to the theater yesterday? When did you have to go to the theater? How did you go to the theater yesterday? Who had to go to the theater yesterday?   have a good seat  He had a good seat in the class. Did he have a good seat in the class? Where did he have a good seat? Who had a good seat in the class? When did he have a good seat in the class?   get angry  He gets angry in the office this morning. When does he get angry in the office? Why does he get angry in the office this morning? Where does he get angry this morning? Who gets angry in the office this morning?   turn round  He always turns round in the class. How often he turns round in the class? Who always turns round in the class? Where does he always turn around?   pay attention  Tom paid attention to the host during the speech. Who paid attention to the host during the speech? Why did he pay attention to the host during the speech? When did he pay attention to the host? Where did he pay attention to the host?   in the end  In the end, we had went to the theater last week. (过去完成时) Had you went to the theater in the end last week? When have you went to the theater in the end? Who had went to the theater in the end?   couldn’t bear it  We couldn’t bear it any more? Could you bear it one more time? How couldn’t you bear it? Why couldn’t you bear it? How can you bear it.   It’s none of your business. 1.  5. Grammar     Drill     Repetition Drill      给出问题和答案。 并使用答案完成句子。
  What did you listen to? The new?  Yes, I listened to the news.   When did he leave? Immediately?  Yes, he left immediately.   Who was sitting behind you? A young man and a young woman.  A young man and a young woman were sitting behind me.   Where did you go last year? To America.  I went to America last year.   Where were they waiting? At the bus stop?  Yes, they were waiting at the bus stop.   How did he open the door? Quietly?  Yes, he opened the door quietly.   When did she receive a letter from his brother? Last week?  Yes, she received a letter from his brother last week.   What did you borrow from the library this morning? A book?  Yes, I borrowed a book from library this morning.   Who spoilt the soup? The cook?  Yes, the cook spoilt the soup.   When did the match end? At four o’clock.  Yes the match ended at four o’clock.    Pattern Drill      训练目标： 写作口语 练习符合英文语序的句子。 T 给出关键字。 S1 使用关键字提问。 S2 使用关键字回答。
 Practice 1
 walk - across the stage - slow.  How did she walk across the stage*? She walked very slowly across the stage?   Behave - at the theater - rude/bad . (形容词二选一)  How did she behave at the theater? She behaved rudely at the theater. She behaved very badly at the theater.   Drive - through the park - quick/slow  How did she drive through the part? She drove quickly through the park. She drove quite slowly through the park.   Sleep - on the train - sound/quiet.  How did she sleep on the train? She slept soundly on the train. She slept very quietly on the train.   Listen - to his story - patient/careful  How did she listen to his story? She listened patiently to his story. She listened carefully to his story.    Practice 2
 Hear the radio  I can hear the radio now. Can you? （提问） Of course I can. I can hear it perfectly well. (注意副词和代词)   hear the actors  I can hear the actors? Can you? Of course I can. I can hear them clearly.   see the theater  I can see the theater now. Could you? Definitely. I could see it clearly.   see her house  I can see her house? Could you? Of course, I can see it perfectly well.   hear his voice  I can hear his voice. could you? Of course I can. I can hear it perfectly well.   see those men  I can see the men now. Can you? Of course I can. I can see them perfectly well.   see the policeman  I can see the policeman now. Can you? Of course I can. I can see him perfectly well.   hear the rain  I can hear the rain now. Can you? Definitely. I can hear it perfectly well.   hear some music  I can hear some music now. Can you? Of course I can. I can hear it perfectly well.    Practice 3
 Last night - a good talk on the radio - saw/heard.  I heard a good talk on the radio last night.   just now - a voice/knock - at the door.  I heard a voice at the door just now. I heard a knock at the door just now.   last night - a cry/shout - outside  I heard a cry outside last night. I heard a shout outside last night.   at lunch - a fly/hair - in my soup  I saw a fly in my soup at lunch. I saw a hair in my soup at lunch.   last week - a camel/monkey - at the zoo.  We saw a camel at the zoo last week. We saw a monkey at the zoo last week.    Practice 4
 see the race - large - crowd  Didn’t you see the race? I couldn’t. The crowd was too large.  crowd 人群 - 视为 单数     read the letter - small/bad - writing  Didn’t you read the letter? I couldn’t. The writing is too small. I couldn’t. The writing is too bad.   see her face - poor/bad - light  Didn’t you see her face? I couldn’t. The light is too poor.  poor 可以形容光线差   I couldn’t. The light is too bad.   swim in the lake - cold/deep - water  Didn’t you swim in the lake? I couldn’t. The water is too cold. I couldn’t. The water is too deep.   finish your lunch - hot/salty - food  Didn’t you finish your lunch. I couldn’t. The food is too hot. I couldn’t. the food is too salty.    5. Comprehension (理解)      根据课文提问并回答。 自问自答。
 6. Asking questions.       As me if What/ When/ How … ? Is / Does …   Practice 2
They were talking loudly. (how)  How were they talking.   I couldn’t hear the actors. (Who)  Who couldn’t hear the actors (I) Who couldn’t you hear (the actors).   I turned around. (What … do)  What did you do?   I looked at the man and the woman angrily. (how)  How did you look at the man and the woman?    7. title: 5. 听力满分计划
content:
Ancient philosophy is not just about talking or lecturing, or even reading long, dense books. In fact, it is something people have used throughout history - to solve their problems and to achieve their greatest triumphs.
Specifically, I am referring to Stoicism, which, in my opinion, is the most practical of all philosophies and therefore the most appealing, Stoicism was founded in Ancient Greece by Zeno of Citium in the early 3rd century BC, but was practised by the likes of Epictetus（埃皮克提图， 哲学家）, Cato, Seneca and Marcus Aurelius. Amazingly, we still have access to these ideas, despite the fact that the most famous Stoics never wrote anything down for publication. Cato definitely didn’t. Marcus Aurelius never intended his Meditations to be anything but personal. Seneca’s letters were, well, letters and Epictetus' thoughts come to us by way of a note-taking student.
Stoic principles were based on the idea that its followers could have an unshakable happiness in this life and the key to achieving this was virtue. The road to virtue, in turn, lay in understanding that destructive emotions, like anger and jealousy, are under our conscious control - they don’t have to control us, because we can learn to control them. In the words of Epictetus: “external events I cannot control, but the choices I make with regard to them, I do control”.
The modern day philosopher and writer Nassim Nicholas Taleb defines a Stoic as someone who has a different perspective on experiences which most of us would see as wholly negative; a Stoic “transforms fear into caution, pain into transformation, mistakes into initiation and desire into undertaking”. Using this definition as a model, we can see that throughout the centuries Stoicism has been practised in more recent history by kings, presidents, artists, writers and entrepreneurs.
The founding fathers of the United States were inspired by the philosophy. George Washington was introduced to Stoicism by his neighbours at age seventeen, and later, put on a play based on the life of Cato to inspire his men. Thomas Jefferson kept a copy of Seneca beside his bed.
Writers and artists have also been inspired by the stoics. Eugene Delacroix, the renowned French Romantic artist (known best for his painting Liberty Leading the People) was an ardent Stoic, referring to it as his “consoling religion”.
The economist Adam Smith’s theories on capitalism（资本主义制度） were significantly influenced by the Stoicism that he studied as a schoolboy, under a teacher who had translated Marcus Aurelius' works.
Today’s political leaders are no different, with many finding their inspiration from the ancient texts. Former US president Bill Clinton rereads Marcus Aurelius every single year, and many have compared former President Obama’s calm leadership style to that of Cato. Wen Jiabao, the former prime minister of China, claims that Meditations is one of two books he travels with and that he has read it more than one hundred times over the course of his life.
Stoicism had a profound influence on Albert Ellis, who invented Cognitive Behaviour Therapy, which is used to help people manage their problems by changing the way that they think and behave. It’s most commonly used to treat depression. The idea is that we can take control of our lives by challenging the irrational beliefs that create our faulty thinking, symptoms and behaviours by using logic instead.
Stoicism has also become popular in the world of business. Stoic principles can build the resilience and state of mind required to overcome setbacks because Stoics teach turning obstacles into opportunity. A lesson every business entrepreneur needs to learn.
I would argue that studying Stoicism is as relevant today as it was 2,000 years ago, thanks to its brilliant insights into how to lead a good life. At the very root of the thinking, there is a very simple way of living - control what you can and accept what you can’t. This is not as easy as it sounds and will require considerable practice - it can take a lifetime to master. The Stoics also believed the most important foundation for a good and happy life is not money, fame, power or pleasure, but having a disciplined and principled character - something which seems to resonate with many people today.

title: a. Let Him Go, Olivia
content:
There I was. Upside down inside the swimming pool. Drowned.
My parents were screaming.
It must have been the summer of ‘63.
It was a gloomy day. Every Sunday we went to my grandparents’ house.
My cousins and I were playing alongside the pool. I must have slipped.
At three years old, I did not know how to swim.
My mother was giving me CPR. More than twenty or twenty-five minutes had gone by. The ambulance had arrived.
Everybody was staring at my mother.
“Let him go, Olivia. It’s over.” Even my father had some feelings of resignation. Yet, she never gave up.
I write this story as a tribute to my mother, who, only four years later, passed away.
And also in recognition of editors who made it possible for my mother to have read in Reader’s Digest the miracle made by another woman utilizing then recently discovered CPR.

title: a. Reading to Learn the Art of Expression
content:
课文     When you read a short story, you may read it merely for pleasure.
When you read a biographical sketch, you may read it merely for information.
But as you are a learner of English, I think you should often read to learn the art of expression.
And for this purpose you may read either a short story or a biographical sketch, either an essay or a news item, indeed, anything that is written in good current English.
Even from a short paragraph, you may learn several forms of expression if you are observant enough.
Try to read the following paragraphs from BBC Modern English and notice the points of usage listed below.
 Over 100 years ago she opened the first British hospital for women.
There are still very few of these hospitals in England.
This hospital is in Euston Road in London.
Its situation means that women from all over England can reach it quite easily.
Her aim when she opened the hospital was to provide a place where women could go and receive treatment from female doctors and nurses.
She also wanted the hospital to provide jobs for female doctors at a time when it was very difficult for them to find work.
Recently the authorities have tried to close the hospital. They say that it is old-fashioned and wastes a lot of money.
However, the Government has decided that the hospital will stay open.
Many people feel very glad that the valuable service offered by this hospital will continue.
 “Over” More than. “in Euston Road” “in … Road”. “means that …” “Means” takes an object clause introduced by “that”. “from all over England” “all over England” “from all over England”. “receive treatment”. Patients receive treatment. “wanted the hospital to provide…” “We want them to do it”. “at a time when …” “at a time when …” “Recently the authorities have tried.” The present perfect is here used with “recently”. “the Government has” “the Government” can be considered singular. “decided that …” “Decide(d)” takes an object clause introduced by “that”. “stay open”. “Stay” can be a copulative verb.   In this way you will learn the art of expression very quickly;
perhaps one or two paragraphs a day will teach you hundreds of forms of expression in a month, and these forms of expression will greatly improve your writing.
And if you can - I believe you can - commit to memory one or two paragraphs a day that you have already read in this way, the results will be still greater.

 Does he make me want to know about little things? Who makes me want to know about little things? Whom does he make want to know about little things? What does he make me want to know?    I wish I knew what kind of the turtle that was. (Who, What)
 (x) Who wish I knew awhat kind fo the turtle that was? (x) What did I wish I know?     这里提问不熟悉。 deepseek 回答。 在 对第一人称提问时， 注意变换对象。

针对 most（程度） 提问时，则不再询问具体内容，而是询问这种愿望的强烈程度，因此用 how much 或 to what extent 来引导问句，同时调整句子的结构，使其语法正确、自然。

We were asked to keep away from the musical instrument, so that it could be repaired by a friend of my father's.  I wish I knew that (尝试查阅 wish 的用法)  wish 表达愿望， 是一个 虚拟语气 语法。
 2.1. 基本结构：wish + 过去式（表示与现在事实相反）
  I wish I knew the answer. (我希望知道， 事实并不知道) I wish my aunt Lucy were not here. (我希望 Lucy 可以下周天来看我， 事实上她现在就来了 N2L2)   2.2. wish + 过去完成式（had + 过去分词）, 表示 对过去已发生之事的后悔或遗憾。
  I wish I had studied harder. 我希望我过去更努力。（实际上没有）。 I wish the female visitor hadn’t touched our clavchord. （我希望那个女游客没有碰我们老钢琴。（事实碰了， 还坏了 N2L10）   2.3. wish + could/would do （对未来的愿望 / 当前的不满）

  I wish/hope you have a nice day.   2.5. wish to do 表示。 陈述愿望。
  I wish to apply for this position. Tim wishes to have a trip in Australia. (N2L4)  sb. figure out sth.   I wish I had figured out why I spent so/that such money last year. (我希望我能搞清楚为什么我去年用了这么多钱。)  你想表达的是：“我现在希望我（在过去）搞清楚了…” 这是一个对过去已发生事件的遗憾。因此，应该使用 wish + 过去完成时 (had done) 的结构。   Did the citizens figure out why the clock stopped? (市民们搞清楚大钟为什么停下来了吗？ N2L9) Finally, we figured out how long the pigeons cost from Pinhurst to Silbury. (最终，我们知道鸽子从 Pinhurst 到 Silury 要飞多久。 N2L5)  Finally, we figured out how long it took the pigeons to fly from Pinhurst to Silbury. (结构解析： figured out 的宾语是 how long it took … to fly 这个整个从句。it 是形式主语，真正的主语是 to fly …)    down to ride … (fully support)   4.1. down to 在口语中表示 “愿意做某事，准备好了，有兴趣参与”，相当于 “in for” 或 “ready and willing”。 4.2. ride 它融合了 “ride with someone”（与某人同行）和 “ride or die”（同生共死、绝对忠诚的伙伴）的含义。 “Ride” 意味着 全程支持、力挺、陪伴某人度过任何挑战，不离不弃。
  Fight it on, Ben. I’m always down to ride for you. (加油干， 本。 我永远支持你。)  不要 always: 因为 down to ride 本身已有“随时准备着”的含义。 Fight on, Ben. I’m down to ride for you Go get ’em, Ben. I’m riding with you.   为什么学英语？ 学英语是为了做什么？
   学英语本身， 遣词造句， 英语起源。    把英语作为工具。 使用英语学习其他专业知识。      目标1. 听说读写      听说读写 （入：听读。 出：说写）
 从其他文章摘抄习惯用法。 精读 - 关注 词语、习惯用法。 泛读 - 关注文章承载的信息。 日积月累。  摘抄+造句+朗读 - 提升听说读写      How?
 如何造句？ 重看 N1-3 如何跟读？ 跟真人语音。 如何摘抄？ //!todo    阅读（一切的基础）单词、语法、习惯用法
 精读能力 - 摘抄 - 提升所有能力。 泛读能力 - 内容 - 提升输出能力（口语和写作）。    雅思托福，怎么准备？
 听说读写， 什么最难准备？  输出（说写）。 输出的基础是输入。   内容 - 言之有物。 （听力+阅读+见闻） 口语的结构 - 逻辑清晰。 基于 阅读和写作 训练 表达 - 高级用法 + 说话情感  单词、语法、 习惯用法 语音、语调、语速、变音、流利度   大量练习，（无意识-有意识-下意识）。 无他，唯手熟尔。     保持良好的心态: 阅读和听力 就是在提升 口语和写作。 学习是一个长期的过程， 日拱一卒， 聚沙成塔。  目标2: 如何学会从阅读材料中摘抄，并造句。      原则: 好词好句 + 自己不会的   那刚开始就会很多吗？ 肯定会， 但慢慢的就越来越少。 （commit to memory 1 or 2 paragraphs a day will teach you hundreds of forms of expression in a month， 积土成山， 为道日损） observant: 慧眼识珠、 仔细.  练习摘抄能力： 自己练习摘抄 + 对比 Leo 的课程。    摘抄的结果用于何处？   造句、写作、 口语练习。 读书破万卷、下笔如有神。 腹有诗书气自华（口语）： 表达  如何提高造句的正确率。   多练、 多模仿。 不要纠结 每一次造句的完全正确。 更应该注重自己成长的提升  准确率更高了。 遣词造句更精妙了。     效果和效率      效果和效率的区别？   效果 是 结果 : 到 北京 效率 是 达成结果所用的时间和消耗的精力: 走路，汽车，飞机 到北京。  如何提升效率？   选择更好的方法 什么是更好的方法？ 能解决本质问题的方法， 能举一反三的方法， 能触类旁通的方法。不是 头痛医头 的方法。 怎么得到更好的方法？ 向别人学习。 （咨询、 讨论、 付费） 有了方法之后怎么办？ 练习、实践、对比前后状态、 总结 （循环）

title: n2l02 - Breakfast or lunch
content:
课前问题       be+doing vs do/does 感叹句？ 如何确定频率副词 adv. 的位置？   Always (100%) → Usually → Often/Frequently → Sometimes → Occasionally → Rarely/Seldom → Hardly ever → Never (0%)
课文     It was Sunday.
I never get up early on Sundays. I sometimes stay in bed until lunch time.
Last Sunday, I got up very late.
I looked out of the window. It’s dark outside.
“What a day!”, I thought, “It’s raining again.”
Just then, the telephone rang.
It was my aunt Lucy.
“I’ve just arrived by train,” she said. “I’m coming to see you.”
“But I’m still having breakfast.” I repeated.
“Dear me”, she said. “Do you [[always]] get up so late? It’s one o’clock.”
Vocabulary      until (adv. 直到…)  I sometimes stay in bed until lunchtime. I usually go to bed until 12p.m. How often do you eat lunch until 1 pm. I couldn’t swim until 21 year-old.   outside (adv. 在外面) / inside (adv. 在里面) – (地点状语 where 提问)  get inside (进来） - get outside （出去)   It’s dark outside. Do you know why it’s dark outside? She occasionally walks along outside. (她偶尔在外面一个人散步)  Where does she occasionally walk along?   There’s a tiger outside. I heard the door knock, what is outside? (我听到敲门声， 什么在外面)   ring (v. 铃响) - rang - rung  Just then, the telephone rang. Did the telephone ring? When did the telephone ring? The telephone is ringing. The bell seldom rings at night.   aunt (n. 阿姨) - uncle (叔叔) – (主语, who)  cousin (表/堂兄弟) -   Your aunt is young and pretty. My aunt rarely visits our family on Sundays. Do you know your aunt, Lucy? Where’s your aunt?   repeat (v. 重复)  repeat after me. Can you repeat your question? (很正式)  Pardon? / What? / Come again? (比较随意)      Grammar     1. 现在进行时 (be + doing)     1.1. 一个动作正在发生      We’re having a conversation. Are you having a conversation. We are not having a conversation.  语法     链接 - #频率 #频率副词 语法 - #过去进行时 #一般现在时
Patten Drill     Practice 1
 John’s sleeping.  Where’s John? He’s late. I think he’s still sleeping.   Mr. Smith’s teaching.  Where Mr. Smith? He’s late. I think he’s still teaching.   Mrs. Smith’s cooking.  Where’s Mrs. Smith? She’s late. I think she’s still cooking.   Henry’s working.  Where’s Henry? He’s late. I think he’s still working.   Mary’s having lunch.  Where’s Mary. She’s late. I think she’s still having lunch.   Jane’s dressing.  Where’s Jane? She’s late. I think she’s still dressing.   Tom’s getting ready. （正在准备）  Where’s Tom. He’s late. I think he’s still getting ready.   Lucy’s telephoning. (正在打电话)  Where’s Lucy? She’s late. I think she’s still telephoning.   James is shaving.  Where’s James? He’s late. I think he’s still shaving.    Practice 2
 clean the car - Sunday.  Why are you cleaning the car now? Because it’s Sunday. I always clean the car on Sundays.   ring your aunt/friend - Saturday.  Why are you ringing your aunt now?  Because it’s Saturday. I always ring her on Saturdays.   Why are your ringing your friend now?  Because it’s Saturday. I always ring him on Saturdays.     go to the library/bank - Friday.  Why are you going to the library now?  Because it’s Friday. I always go to the library on Fridays.   Why are you going to the bank now?  Because it’s Friday. I always go to the back on Fridays.     play football/tennis - Wednesday.  Why are you playing football now?  Because it’s Wednesday. I always play football on Wednesdays.   Why are you playing tennis now?  Because it’s Wednesday. I always play tennis on Wednesdays.     write to John/Mary - Thursday.  Why are you writing to John now?  Because it’s Thursday. I always write to him on Thursdays.   Why are your writing to Mary now?  Because it’s Thursday. I always write to her on Thursdays.      Practice 3
 现在进行时表示最近一段时间的状态。
  drive very fast  He’s driving very fast these days. He doesn’t usually drive very fast.   drink heavily (酗酒/ 醉酒)  He’s drinking heavily these days. He doesn’t usually drink heavily.   write carefully  He’s writing carefully these days. He doesn’t usually write carefully.   walk slowly  She’s walking slowly these days. She doesn’t usually write carefully.   sleep soundly  He’s sleeping soundly these days. He doesn’t usually sleep soundly.   cook well  Tom’s cooking well these days. Tom doesn’t usually cook well.   get up early  He’s getting up early these days. He doesn’t usually get up early.   work hard  He’s working hard these days. He doesn’t usually work hard.   stay in bed late  He’s staying in bed late recently. He doesn’t usually stay in bed late.    Practice 4
 rude people  What rude people. Yes, they are rude, aren’t they!   an ugly woman  What an ugly woman! Yes, she is ugly, isn’t she!   a strange story  What a strange story! Yes, it is strange, isn’t it!   wonderful actors  What wonderful actors! Yes, they are wonderful, aren’t they.   an interesting play  What an interesting play! Yes, it is interesting, isn’t it!   horrible dresses  What horrible dresses! Yes, they are horrible, aren’t they.   a rude girl  What a rude girl! Yes, she’s rude, isn’t she.   a good party  What a good party! Yes, it’s good, isn’t it!   an amusing man  What an amusing man! Yes, he’s amusing, isn’t he.

title: z. 形容词 `then` 用法详解
content:
核心概念     这里的 then 不是副词“然后”，而是形容词“当时的”。
原句分析      原短语： then recently discovered CPR 字面意思： “在当时那个时间点，新近被发现的心肺复苏术” 结构： then（形容词） + recently discovered（复合形容词） + CPR（名词）  语法功能       时间锚定作用
then 将“新发现”的时间锁定在故事发生的过去时刻，而不是作者写作的现在时刻。
  双重时间限定
 recently discovered：相对于某个时间点“最近” then：明确指出这个时间点是故事中的1963年    拆解理解      Without then: 新近发现的CPR（可能指现在的新发现） With then: 在当时（1963年） 算是新近发现的CPR  同义转换      …utilizing CPR, which was, at that time, a recently discovered technique.
 常见类似结构        短语 含义     the then president 当时的总统   my then boyfriend 我当时的男朋友   the then popular theory 当时流行的理论   in the then capital 在当时的首都    记忆技巧     公式： then + 形容词短语/名词 = “当时的…”
检验方法： 可以在 then 位置换成 “at that time” 或 “at the time” 来理解：
 the then president → the president at that time then recently discovered → recently discovered at that time   在原故事中的具体作用     作者站在现在回忆1963年：
CPR在更早（50年代末）被研发，但对1963年的事件来说，它仍是“新”技术。
then 精准定位了这个“新”是相对于1963年，而不是写作的现在。

title: z2 长难句解析
content:
And also in recognition of editors who made it possible for my mother to have read in Reader’s Digest the miracle made by another woman utilizing then recently discovered CPR.
如何断句断句（“翻译 + 结构图”）     意思：
这句话在表达—— “同时也为了表彰那些编辑，是他们让我的母亲能够在《读者文摘》上读到另一位女性使用当时新发现的心肺复苏术创造的奇迹。”
结构图：
 in recognition of editors  who made it possible  for my mother  to have read  in Reader’s Digest the miracle  made by another woman  utilizing then recently discovered CPR              为什么 in Reader’s Digest 必须放在 have read 后面？      I found this sentence in a book, but I find it a bit difficult to break it into meaningful chunks while reading. Especially the phrase ‘in Reader’s Digest’ after ‘have read’. I feel it might make more sense if it were moved to the end of the sentence.
 关键原因： 英语中“阅读在哪里”通常紧跟在动词 read 后面。 位置关系是：

 如果你把它放到句尾，就会变成：
 … the miracle … in Reader’s Digest.
 这会产生歧义： 好像 the miracle 是在 Reader’s Digest 中发生的，而不是“阅读发生在 Reader’s Digest 上”。
因此：

title: z3. in recognition of sb/sth
content:
“In recognition of my teachers” 在句子中属于“状语”（Adverbial），具体来说是“状语中的目的状语”或“原因状语”。
 1. 在新概念六部分分析法中的位置     你提到的 Subject（主语）, Verb（动词）, Object（宾语）, How（方式）, Where（地点）, When（时间） 是一个非常好的基础句型分析框架。但这个框架主要覆盖核心成分和最常见的状语。
“In recognition of…” 这个短语，不属于主语、动词或宾语这些核心成分。它是一个 额外的、补充说明性的成分，我们可以把它理解为 “Why”（原因）或 “For what purpose”（目的）。
虽然“How, Where, When”是常见的状语类别，但状语家族很庞大，还包括：
  原因状语 (Adverbial of Reason) - Why?
  目的状语 (Adverbial of Purpose) - For what purpose?
  条件状语 (Adverbial of Condition) - Under what condition?
  让步状语 (Adverbial of Concession) - Despite what?
  “In recognition of…” 就是一个典型的“原因/目的状语”。
例句分析：
 In recognition of my teachers' hard work, I dedicate this award to them.
  主语 (S): I
  动词 (V): dedicate
  宾语 (O): this award
(到这里，核心意思已经完整：我献上这个奖。)
  状语 - 给谁 (间接宾语/方式): to them
  状语 - 原因/目的 (Why): In recognition of my teachers' hard work
   所以，在你的分析框架里，它可以被归入一个扩展的“Why”的部分。
 2. 更通用的语法成分分析（状语）     在现代语法分析中，我们更常这样说：
  “In recognition of my teachers” 是一个 介词短语。
  这个介词短语在整个句子里充当 状语，修饰整个句子或谓语动词，说明动作的 原因或目的。
  它非常灵活，可以放在句首、句中或句末。
  位置示例：
  句首（最强调这个原因）：
 In recognition of my teachers, I will donate the prize money to the school’s scholarship fund.
（为了表彰我的老师们，我将把奖金捐给学校奖学金基金。）
   句中（紧跟主语之后，语气自然）：
 I, in recognition of my teachers, owe my success to their guidance.
（我，为了表彰我的老师们，将我的成功归功于他们的指导。）
   句末（作为补充说明）：
 I accept this honor humbly, in recognition of all my teachers.
（我谦卑地接受这份荣誉，以表彰我所有的老师。）
    3. 关键理解：“In recognition of” 的核心含义     这个短语的难点在于，“recognition”是名词，但整个短语表达的是一个 动作或状态的目的。
  字面意思： “出于对…的认可/表彰”
  功能意思： “为了表彰…” 、 “为了感谢…” 、 “鉴于…”
  = To recognize…
  = To show gratitude for…
  = Because I recognize…
    把它理解为一个更正式、更书面的 “To thank…” 或 “Because of…”，就能明白它的状语功能了。
总结        你的问题 答案     属于什么成分？ 状语（具体是原因或目的状语）   在 S+V+O+How+Where+When 框架里？ 属于扩展的 “Why” 部分。   本质是什么？ 一个表示 “为了表彰/感谢…” 的介词短语。   如何造句？ 把它当作一个表示原因的“块”，放在句首、主语后或句末，用逗号隔开通常更清晰。    简单造句练习：
 In recognition of your help, I bought you a gift. (Why did I buy it? 原因)
为了感谢你的帮助，我给你买了礼物。
 现在清楚了吗？你可以试着用这个结构造个句，我来帮你检查。
强烈的情感色彩（郑重）     你提出的这个句子 “In recognition of his help, I lent him 20 pounds.” 非常有意思，它触及了 “in recognition of” 这个短语最核心的语用和情感色彩问题。
从纯语法和字面意思上看，这个句子完全正确。但它听起来不太自然，甚至有点奇怪。原因在于语义和语用上的不匹配。
 问题分析：为何听起来“奇怪”？       情感与行为的“价值错配”
  “In recognition of” 传达的是一种正式的、郑重的、带有荣誉性质的感谢或表彰。它常用于重大成就、长期奉献、深刻影响等场合。
  “Lent him 20 pounds” (借给他20英镑) 是一个具体的、小额的经济往来行为。
  将如此正式的感谢语用在一笔小额借款上，感觉像是 “用典礼级的礼节去感谢别人帮你递了支笔”，显得小题大做 (overkill) 或带有反讽 (ironic) 意味。
    更自然的表达方式
对于这种日常、具体的帮助，更地道的说法是：
  To thank him for his help, I lent him 20 pounds. (为了感谢他的帮助，我借了他20英镑。)
  As a thank-you for his help, I lent him 20 pounds. (作为对他帮助的感谢，我借了他20英镑。)
  Because he helped me, I lent him 20 pounds. (因为他帮了我，所以我借了他20英镑。)
     如何修正？两个方向     方向一：如果要保留“in recognition of”，必须提升“帮助”的层级和价值。
 In recognition of his invaluable help during my financial crisis, I offered him an interest-free loan.
（为感谢他在我财务危机时提供的宝贵帮助，我向他提供了一笔无息贷款。）
  说明： 将“帮助”具体化为 “invaluable help during my financial crisis”，将“借款”提升为 “an interest-free loan”，这样价值和精神层面就匹配了。  方向二：如果要保留“lent 20 pounds”这个事实，必须更换更口语化的开头。
 To show my appreciation for his help, I lent him 20 pounds when he was short.
（为了表达对他帮助的感谢，在他缺钱时我借了他20英镑。）
  说明： 用 “To show my appreciation for…” 完美替代，情感程度恰到好处。  总结与对比        你的原句 问题 修改建议     In recognition of his help, I lent him 20 pounds. 用词过重，价值不匹配。听起来可能像客气过头，或者有反讽意味。 1. 提升帮助和回馈的价值。 2. 将开头换成 “To thank him for…” 或 “To show my appreciation for…”。    结论：
这个句子是一个绝佳的例子，说明学英语不仅要学语法正确，更要学使用得体。In recognition of 是一个“高规格”的表达，需要与之匹配的“高规格”语境。对于日常小忙，更简单直接的 to thank/thank you for 才是更自然的选择。
你提出了一个非常棒的观察！这说明你对这个短语的用法已经有了很深的敏感度。

title: 针对频率进行提问
content:
针对 频率进行提问 副词提问，需要使用一个专门的疑问词：How often
 1. 基本句型结构：
How often + 助动词/情态动词/be动词 + 主语 + 主要动词？
2. 根据原句时态和动词类型进行转换：
  原句有 be 动词：
  陈述句：She is always late.
  疑问句：How often is she late? (她多久迟到一次？)
    原句有助动词/情态动词：
  陈述句：You can usually find him in the library.
  疑问句：How often can you find him in the library?
    原句只有行为动词/系动词（最常见的情况）：
  陈述句：She always looks good. / He goes to the gym.
  疑问句：How often does she look good? / How often does he go to the gym?
  关键： 需要添加助动词 do/does/did，并将主要动词变回原形。
    3. 回答方式：
回答 How often 的问题，就是用表示频率的副词或短语。
  频率副词： always, usually, often, sometimes, seldom, rarely, never
  频率短语：
  次数 + 时间： once a week (每周一次), three times a day (一天三次), every day (每天), every other day (每隔一天)
  介词短语： on weekends (在周末), from time to time (不时地)
  句型：As often as I can. (尽可能经常。)
    4. 对比其他“How”开头的问句：
避免与以下问题混淆：
  How long? → 问“时间长度”或“物体长度”。 (How long have you lived here? / How long is the river?)
  How soon? → 问“多快（将来）”。 (How soon will you finish? 你多久能完成？)
  How many times? → 问“具体次数”（通常针对已完成动作）。 (How many times have you been to Beijing? 你去过北京几次了？)
  总结：
对频率提问，有且几乎只有一个万能问法：How often...?
练习：
请将以下句子改为对频率提问的问句：
  I check my email twice a day.
  They are rarely at home on Sundays.
  My brother has never been abroad.
  答案：
  How often do you check your email?
  How often are they at home on Sundays?
  How often has your brother been abroad?
  ever 怎么用在问句里？
问得非常好！ever 在问句中的用法非常关键，它让问题从询问“具体频率”转变为询问“有无经历”或“任何情况”。
你可以把 ever 理解为 “在任何时候”，它拓宽了时间的范围，涵盖了从过去到现在（甚至将来）的全部时间段。
 一、核心用法与句型     ever 主要用在疑问句和否定句中。在疑问句里，它的核心作用是：
  询问“是否有过某种经历”（最常见）
  在条件、比较等句型中加强语气，意为“究竟、到底、曾经”。
  基本句型结构：
Ever 放在主语之后，主要动词之前。
 二、主要用法分类与例句     1. 询问经历（最核心的用法）     相当于中文的“曾经……过吗？”。常与现在完成时连用，但也可用于过去时或其他时态。
  现在完成时（最典型）：
  Have you ever been to Paris?（你曾经去过巴黎吗？）
  Has she ever tried sushi?（她曾经尝过寿司吗？）
   对比：How often have you been to Paris? (询问频率：你去过巴黎几次？)
    Have you ever been to Paris? (询问经历：你去过（一次）巴黎吗？)
   一般过去时（也常见）：
  Did you ever meet him when you worked there?（你在那里工作时，见过他吗？）
   现在完成时强调经历与现在的关联，一般过去时只是单纯询问过去某个时间段是否发生过。
     一般现在时（多用于询问习惯或普遍可能性）：
  Do you ever go hiking?（你（平时）会去徒步吗？）
  Does this ever happen?（这种事会发生吗？）
    2. 用于特殊疑问句，加强语气（意为“究竟、到底”）     这时 ever 跟在疑问词（what, who, why, how 等）后面，合在一起使用，表示惊讶、不耐烦或强调。
  What ever are you doing? = What on earth are you doing?（你到底在干什么？）
  How ever did you manage to finish it?（你究竟是怎么完成的？）
  Why ever didn‘t you call me?（你到底为什么不打电话给我？）
   注意：口语中常写成一个词：whatever, whoever, however，但在正式语法中，分开写强调语气更强。
   3. 用于比较级和最高级句型       比较级： It‘s raining harder than ever (before).（雨下得比以往任何时候都大。）
  最高级： This is the best movie I have ever seen.（这是我看过的最好电影。）【注意：此句虽为肯定陈述句，但内含一个隐含的“经历”范围，是 ever 可用于肯定句的少数情况之一】
  4. 用于条件句和否定句       条件句： If you ever need help, just call me.（如果你任何时候需要帮助，就打电话给我。）
  否定句（与 never 同义，但语气更强）： I will never ever forget you. 或 I won‘t ever forget you.（我永远永远不会忘记你。）
   三、重要注意事项       与 How often 的区别（你之前问题的延伸）
  How often…? → 问 频率 (多常？多久一次？)
  …ever…? → 问 经历 (曾经……过吗？)
  例句对比：
  How often do you travel?（你多久旅行一次？）-> 回答：Once a year.
  Do you ever travel? / Have you ever traveled abroad?（你（曾经）旅行过吗？/你出过国吗？）-> 回答：Yes, I have. / No, never.
      在肯定陈述句中慎用
  Ever 通常不用于普通的肯定陈述句。
  错误： I ever went to London.
  正确： I have been to London. 或 I once went to London.
  例外： 如上面提到的“最高级”结构，以及一些固定搭配如 ever since（自从……以来）。
    与 Never 的问答
  对含有 ever 的疑问句做否定回答，最常用的词就是 never。
  Q: Have you ever seen a ghost?
  A: No, I never have. / No, never.
    总结表格：
   疑问词/用法 核心含义 例句     How often…? 询问频率（多久一次） How often do you exercise?   …ever…? 询问经历（曾经……过吗） Do you ever exercise? / Have you ever run a marathon?   What/How/Why ever…? 加强语气（到底、究竟） How ever did you find it?   the + 最高级 + … ever 表示“有史以来最……” She is the kindest person I have ever met.    希望这个更系统的解释能帮助你完全掌握 ever 在问句中的用法！
ever 只能和一般疑问句吗？
非常好的问题！你的直觉很准，答案是否定的。Ever 不仅能用于一般疑问句，它在特殊疑问句中也极其常见且重要。
我们可以把它分为两大类：
一、在一般疑问句中：询问“有无经历”     这是你最初想到的用法，也是最基础的。
  Do you ever feel lonely?（你有时会感到孤独吗？）
  Has he ever been to Japan?（他去过日本吗？）
   二、在特殊疑问句中：询问“经历的具体细节”     这是非常关键的进阶用法。此时 ever 不再直接跟在助动词后，而是跟在特殊疑问词之后、主语之前。 它把问题从“是否发生过”升级为“何时/何地/如何/为何发生过”。
结构：疑问词 + ever + 助动词 + 主语 … ?
对比一下，区别一目了然：
  询问时间
  一般疑问：Have you ever met a celebrity?（你见过名人吗？）
  特殊疑问：**When** did you ever meet a celebrity?（你到底什么时候见过名人？）【问具体时间】
  特殊疑问：**When** have you ever done that before?（你以前什么时候做过这种事？）【强调“从未有过”的质疑语气】
    询问地点
  一般疑问：Have you ever traveled abroad?（你出国旅行过吗？）
  特殊疑问：**Where** have you ever seen such a beautiful view?（你在哪儿见过这么美的景色？）【常用于反问，暗示“从未见过”】
    询问方式
  一般疑问：Did he ever finish the project?（他完成过那个项目吗？）
  特殊疑问：**How** did you ever manage to solve it?（你到底是怎么设法解决的？）【加强惊叹语气】
    询问原因
  一般疑问：Would you ever lie to me?（你会对我撒谎吗？）
  特殊疑问：**Why** would you ever say such a thing?（你怎么会说出这种话？）【加强震惊、不赞同的语气】
    询问人物
  一般疑问：Have you ever told anyone?（你告诉过任何人吗？）
  特殊疑问：**Who** have you ever trusted completely?（你曾经完全信任过谁？）
     三、两种用法的核心区别        特征 在一般疑问句中 在特殊疑问句中     目的 询问是否存在某种经历或可能性。 1. 询问经历的具体细节（何时、何地等）。 2. 作为修辞性反问，表达惊讶、质疑或否定（这是非常地道的用法）。   回答 通常用 Yes/No，或 Yes, once. / No, never. 必须提供具体信息，或本身就是一种（否定性的）情绪表达。   语气 中性、单纯的询问。 常常带有强烈的感情色彩（惊讶、不耐烦、难以置信）。   例句 Have you ever been to Italy?（你去过意大利吗？） When have you ever listened to my advice?（你什么时候听过我的话？）【言下之意：你从未听过】    特别注意： 当 ever 用于特殊疑问句时，有时并非真正期待一个答案，而是作为一种修辞手法，强调“从未”或“难以想象”。
  What did he ever do to deserve this?（他到底做了什么配得上这个？）【暗示他没做什么】
  How could you ever forgive him?（你怎么可能原谅他？）【表示难以置信】
  总结     Ever 是一个非常灵活的词：
  在 一般疑问句 中，它拓宽时间范围，询问“有无”。
  在 特殊疑问句 中，它：
  继续拓宽时间范围，用于询问具体细节。
  更重要的是，它经常为句子注入强烈的情绪，表达惊讶、质疑或否定，这是语言地道性的一个关键点。
    所以，请务必记住：ever 绝不局限于一般疑问句，它在特殊疑问句中的作用同样强大且常用。

针对 频率进行提问 副词提问，需要使用一个专门的疑问词：How often
 1. 基本句型结构：
How often + 助动词/情态动词/be动词 + 主语 + 主要动词？
2. 根据原句时态和动词类型进行转换：
  原句有 be 动词：
  陈述句：She is always late.
  疑问句：How often is she late? (她多久迟到一次？)
    原句有助动词/情态动词：
  陈述句：You can usually find him in the library.
  疑问句：How often can you find him in the library?
    原句只有行为动词/系动词（最常见的情况）：
  陈述句：She always looks good.

频率副词 - 表示频率的 副词
频率从高到低     高频: 1. always(总是 100%), 2. constantly / continually (持续不断的， 强调 持续状态 3. frequently (频繁的)
中频: 4. usually (通常 90%), 5. generally / normally / regularly （通常， 一般地， 定期地） 6. often （经常 60-70%)
中低频: 7. sometimes (有时 40-50%） 8. occasionally (偶尔 30%)
低频: 9. rarely / seldom (很少， 罕有 10%) 10. hardly ever / almost never （几乎不， 1%） 11. never （从不 0%）
merely (仅仅，只不过) - 不是频率副词。 表示程度或范围。 + I merely suggested it. 我只是建议一下。
针对频率的提问     [[how-to-ask-frequency]]
频率副词在句子中的位置      v. 前 be 后 有例外  sometimes 可以在句子任何位置。    Practice
 Do you ever get up early on Sundays? (Never)  I never get up early on Sundays.   Do you speed your holidays abroad? (Sometimes) 任意位置  Sometimes I spend my holidays abroad. I spend my holidays abroad sometimes. I sometimes spend my holidays abroad.   Does he answer your letters? (Rarely)  He rarely answers my letters.   Do you and Tom ever have lunch at this restaurant? (Frequently)  Tom and I frequently have lunch at this restaurant.   Do the children play football in the street? (Always)  They always play football in the street.   Do you ever buy CDs? (often)  I often buy CDs?   Do his friends ever visit him? (Seldom, 几乎不， 表示否定)  His friends seldom visit him.   Does he ever go to the theater? (Occasionally)  He occasionally goes to the theater.   Does your aunt come to see you on Sundays? (Generally)  She generally comes to see me on Sundays.   Does Joe get up late on Sundays. (Usually)  He usually gets up late on Sundays.    expression
